texts.preamble: Sita Ram vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 31 October, 2018 Author: Tarlok Singh Chauhan Bench: Tarlok Singh Chauhan In The High Court Of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla . Cr.MMO No. 46 of 2018. Date of decision: 31.10.2018. Sita Ram .....Petitioner. Versus State of Himachal Pradesh ..... Respondent. Coram The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Tarlok Singh Chauhan, Judge. Whether approved for reporting?1No For the Petitioners : Mr. R.S. Chandel, Advocate. For the Respondent : Mr. Vinod Thakur and Mr. Sudhir Bhatnagar, Addl. A.Gs., with Mr. Rajat Chauhan, Law Officer. Tarlok Singh Chauhan, Judge (Oral).
texts.facts: The petitioner takes exception to the order passed by learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Theog on 13.11.2017 whereby his application seeking impleadment of the manufacturer and distributor of the Haldi Powder recovered from his shop, upon which prosecution has been launched against him under Section 16(1) (a) (I) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short 'Act'), has filed this petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure assailing the said order. 2. A complaint has been filed against the petitioner under Section . 16(1) (a) (i) of the Act, which is pending adjudication before the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Theog and is fixed for recording the statement of the petitioner under Section 313 Cr.P.C. Sita Ram vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 31 October, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113840528/ 1 3. In the complaint filed against the petitioner, it was alleged that he was proprietor of 'Sharma General Store' Bhakelti and on 29.4.2010 the Food Inspector had inspected the shop and took the samples of six packets of Haldi Powder and after sealing the same as per the procedure sent them for analysis wherein the samples have been found to be adulterated, resulting in launching of the prosecution against the petitioner. 4. It is during the fag end of the proceedings that the petitioner filed an application under Section 20A of the Act seeking impleadment of the alleged distributor and manufacturer of the Haldi Powder recovered from his premises. However, the said application, as observed above, has been dismissed primarily on the ground that the petitioner had not brought on record any document whereby it could be gathered that the Haldi in fact had been purchased from the alleged distributor i.e. Brahma Nand Vijay Kumar, Shalli Bazar, Theog, District Shimla, H.P. and, therefore, on the same analogy the prayer for impleading the alleged manufacturer was also declined.
texts.arguments: 5. It is vehemently argued by Mr. R.S.Chandel, learned counsel for the petitioner that the orders passed by the learned trial Magistrate is based on surmises and conjectures as the name of the manufacturer was clearly printed . on Ext.CW-1/C that had been produced before the Court. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the material placed on record. 6. Once the petitioner himself had not sought the impleadment of manufacturer, obviously the trial Magistrate could not have suo motu impleaded the so called manufacturer even if the name was found to be contained in Ex.C-1 as alleged because it was for the petitioner to have first proved on record that he had purchased the samples from the distributor and it is only if the distributor had, in turn, named the manufacturer, then alone could such manufacturer as named by the distributor be impleaded as a party . because the cases are not lacking where the names of the reputed manufacturers are found printed on the labels, whereas the products are not manufactured by the named manufacturer and are rather manufactured by the counterfeit manufacturer.
